chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ibn Abi Nasr from Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Muqri from Ubayd Allah ibn Musa al-Absi from Isra'il ibn Yunus from Ishaq al-Sabii from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) said:
"The one who is al-musta lat (from the ritual of al-la'an) does not inherit and is not inherited from, and he is called to his father."

key_terms.الْمُسْتَلاَطُ: The child resulting from the ritual of al-la'an (mutual cursing)
key_terms.يُدْعَى إِلَى أَبِيهِ: Is called/attached to his father (lineage attribution)

ai.seo_question: What are the inheritance rules for a child of al-la'an in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the specific inheritance status of the *mustalat* (child of *mula'ana*) in Shia jurisprudence, establishing that while the child is not an heir to the father nor does the father inherit from the child, the child's lineage remains attached to the father. This ruling distinguishes the *mustalat* from other categories of offspring, ensuring the father retains his paternal rights and obligations despite the formal separation of inheritance ties. The narration underscores the precision of Shia legal theory in handling complex familial relationships arising from the *mula'ana* procedure.
